name: MathlibAnnex.IsometryEquiv.map_center_of_mapsTo_pointReflection
title: Center transport under bounded point-reflection symmetry

content.display_title: Center transport under bounded point-reflection symmetry
content.one_sentence_role: Uses a doubling argument to identify the reflection centers under a bijective isometry.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $X,Y$ be real normed affine spaces, with translation spaces $V,W$. For $c\in X$, point reflection about $c$ is $\sigma_c(x)=c-(x-c)$; define $\sigma_d$ on $Y$ similarly. Let $S\subseteq X$, $T\subseteq Y$, choose $c\in S$ and $d\in T$, and let $f:S\to T$ be a bijective isometry. If $S$ is bounded and $\sigma_c(S)\subseteq S$, $\sigma_d(T)\subseteq T$, then $f(c)=d$.
content.assumptions: The metrics come from the normed translation spaces $V,W$. The centers belong to their respective subsets; $S$ is bounded; and each subset is invariant under reflection about its designated center. No convexity, openness, completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is used.
content.conclusion: The given isometry sends the designated source center to the designated target center: $f(c)=d$.
content.proof_summary: A conjugation argument doubles the displacement of a center under a self-isometry. Boundedness forces that displacement to vanish; applying the result to the transported target reflection identifies the two centers.
proof_steps: Point reflection is an involutive isometry and fixes its center. Hence the two invariance assumptions restrict $\sigma_c$ and $\sigma_d$ to bijective isometries of $S$ and $T$; this is [Restriction of point reflection](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/Reflection.lean#L23-L36).

For a bijective self-isometry $g:S\to S$, define $$\Gamma(g)=\sigma_c\circ g^{-1}\circ\sigma_c\circ g.$$ Since $\sigma_c(c)=c$, distance preservation gives $$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{dist}(\Gamma(g)(c),c)&=\operatorname{dist}(g^{-1}(\sigma_c(g(c))),c)\\&=\operatorname{dist}(\sigma_c(g(c)),g(c))\\&=2\operatorname{dist}(g(c),c).\end{aligned}$$ This is the doubling calculation in [Bounded reflection-center lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/Reflection.lean#L38-L72).

The set of numbers $\operatorname{dist}(g(c),c)$ is bounded because both points lie in bounded $S$. Let $C$ be its supremum. Since $\Gamma(g)$ is again a self-isometry of $S$, Step 2 yields $2\operatorname{dist}(g(c),c)\le C$ for every $g$, hence $2C\le C$ and therefore $C=0$. Thus every self-isometry of $S$ fixes $c$.

Apply the preceding result to $g=f^{-1}\circ\sigma_d\circ f$. Then $$f^{-1}(\sigma_d(f(c)))=c,$$ so $\sigma_d(f(c))=f(c)$. A point is fixed by reflection about $d$ only when it equals $d$; equivalently, $f(c)-d=-(f(c)-d)$. Hence $f(c)=d$.
